comment: The Academy at Alexandria: a solo, offline act every character plays before the server. Places, Instructors, the cohort's name pools and temperaments, and the lessons. Every line is the owner's to rewrite. In lines: {name} is the player's character; {my_name}, {my_shape}, {my_blood}, {my_city} are the speaker's own; {your_shape}, {your_blood} the player's.

arrival.speaker: varga
lines: There you are. You're taller. A year does that.

This is Alexandria: the thirteenth fortress, built around the Library. The Academy is the upper city. Everyone who wakes on the line comes here, from every city, which is why you'll never again stand in a room this mixed.

Nobody dies here, {name}. The whole fortress is warded; the yard doubly. Break your arm, break your pride, break a Term if you're foolish, and the wards will hold you. Out on the line there are no wards. That's what the term is for.
Your cohort is in the quad. Go and meet them. Then the Yardmaster wants you in the yard: your first lesson is Hold.

doors.label: the Gate
doors.locked: The line leaves from the Gate at Commencement. Not before.

doors.label: the Hearth Hall
doors.locked: The rite is held in the Hearth Hall. The Instructors will call you when it is time: after your first lesson, and a night's rest.

doors.label: the Instructors' Tower
doors.locked: The Instructors' Tower. Students go up when they are sent for.

doors.label: the Post, ahead
doors.locked: The cutting is not clear. Fell what hunts in it.

doors.label: the line back
doors.locked: Not with the Warden still standing.

instructors.name: Instructor Ilse Varga
instructors.title: Read · the Instructor who found you

lines.before:hold: The Yardmaster is waiting. West door. Don't make him come and get you; he enjoys it.
lines.after:hold: Bask says you held. He doesn't say that. Rest tonight; tomorrow the hearth.
lines.default: Go on. The Academy rewards the ones who walk about in it.
lines.before:rite: The hearth is lit. North door, when you're ready. Everyone in your cohort has been through it this morning but you. No pressure.
lines.after:rite: So that's what you are. Good. Now we teach you to use it.
lines.after:shape: Bask says you stood up to the cohort. He also says one of them nearly had you. Which is how it should be.
lines.after:discipline: Three techniques and a weapon you chose. That's a Discipline: the first thing about you that your city gave you on purpose.
lines.before:line: Lesson 5. You have held, you have a Shape, you have a school. Now the line, which does not care about any of that.
lines.after:line: You went out and you came back, all three of you. Write that down somewhere; it will not always be true.
lines.after:project: Your field reaches past you now. Everything from here is learning what to do with that. Tomorrow, the Gate.

lines.before:hold: You're Varga's. Good. That one is Millstone, my genius. He is going to bite you a great many times today. Ready?
lines.after:hold: Come back and spar whenever you like. Millstone has taken a liking to you; that is not a compliment.
lines.default: The yard is open. The wards are up. Hit something.
lines.after:rite: Heard the bowl had something to say about you. It usually does.
lines.before:shape: Heard the bowl. So you're a {your_shape} now, whatever you walked in as. Good: today we find out what that means with a weapon in your hand. And then your cohort gets a turn at you.
lines.after:shape: You took the ladder. Some of them will want it back; let them come. Tomorrow Varga's people take you for Discipline.
lines.after:discipline: Rourke, Tane, Halloway: they all say the same thing about their own. That you're sloppy, and that you'll do.
lines.after:line: First run. You look it. Good.
lines.before:project: Varga says the field can go past the skin. She would; she's a Read, hers goes everywhere. Fine. We'll do it her way: stance up, field full, and hold until something gives.
lines.after:project: Stage three, and the Green behind you twice. You're not a first-year any more. Don't tell the first-years.

lines.before:discipline: Columbia sent you, so Columbia teaches you. I am Rourke. A Marshal's field is the law with a hand on it: you name the thing, and then you end it. Weapon first.
lines.after:discipline: You'll do. Serve your first Writ and we'll talk about a commission.
lines.default: The school is open to Columbia's. The rest of you may watch.

lines.before:discipline: River child. Good. I'm Tane. A Pilot's field reads the water and then puts a line across it; everything else is pulling. Choose what you'll pull with.
lines.after:discipline: You read well. The river will teach you the rest, and it does not use the wards.
lines.default: Cahokia's own, step up. Others, keep off my current.

lines.before:discipline: Lunden's, are you? Halloway. Aeronauts fall for a living: the line, the drop, the vent. Everything we do is deciding how to land. Pick what you'll land holding.
lines.after:discipline: You landed on your feet. Most don't, the first week.
lines.default: The school's for Lunden's fog-born. Mind the ballast.

lines.greet: I'm {my_name}. {my_city}, {my_blood}. I think I'm a {my_shape}, but the rite will say. I've read everything the Library lets first-years read. Twice.
lines.after:hold: You did the Millstone drill already? What did he do on the fifth bite? I want to be ready.
lines.after:rite: The bowl took longer with you than with anyone. I timed it. Is that good? I think that's good.
lines.after:shape: I watched your bout. Your stance drops when you reach. Mine does too; I wrote it down.
lines.after:discipline: Which did you choose? For your weapon. I changed mine and now I can't stop thinking I was wrong.
lines.after:line: You chose a party. Did you... think about who? I'd have come. I'd have been useful. Probably.
lines.after:project: Stage three! I measured mine: two paces and a hand. What's yours? Is it rude to ask?

lines.greet: {my_name}. Pleasure. Don't tell anyone, but I woke up in a privy. The field does not choose its moments.
lines.after:hold: You've got the yard look. Sort of a limp, but proud of it.
lines.after:rite: Your genius looked at me. I've decided we're friends now, it and I. You can come too.
lines.after:shape: So that's what a {your_shape} looks like angry. Noted. Filed. Will not be sparring you before breakfast.
lines.after:discipline: Your Instructor shouted your name across the yard. Twice. I think that's affection, in their school.
lines.after:line: Heard the Warden got a look at you. Heard it blinked first.
lines.after:project: Your field's open. I can tell because my hair stands up when you walk past. Flattering, in a way.

lines.greet: {my_name} of {my_city}. My family has sent a child here every generation for three hundred years. You're the recruit Varga brought in herself? Hm.
lines.after:hold: So you held. Everyone holds against a genius that's being kind to them.
lines.after:rite: My family's bowl reading took four seconds. Yours was... theatrical.
lines.after:shape: You beat the ladder. Against first-years. I'll be at the top of it next week; do come.
lines.after:discipline: My school has produced forty Masters. Yours has produced... you, so far. Early days.
lines.after:line: A Green run with a rescue team on standby is a walk with a picnic. Still. You came back.
lines.after:project: Stage three is the floor, not the ceiling. My grandmother reached four at nineteen. Still. Passed, then.

lines.greet: Oh. Hello. I'm {my_name}. Sorry. Everyone here already seems to know what they are. I'm {my_blood}, and that's about all I'm sure of.
lines.after:hold: Does it hurt? The yard? Varga said the wards stop it hurting, but she says a lot of things kindly.
lines.after:rite: I closed my eyes for mine. I watched all of yours. It was beautiful. Is that strange to say?
lines.after:shape: I lost in eleven seconds. I counted. But the wards caught me and nobody laughed, so. Maybe again tomorrow.
lines.after:discipline: The Instructor's test. Did you win? I fell off the ring. Technically that's a loss. Technically.
lines.after:line: Was it bad? Out there? You can tell me if it was bad. I'd rather know.
lines.after:project: You passed the Examination. The real one. I go out next week. Will you... tell me what the post is like?

lines.greet: You're new off the line too? I'm {my_name}. If you need anything, the {my_shape} bunks are by the east wall and I don't sleep much.
lines.after:hold: You look done in. There's bread in the dormitory; I saved you some.
lines.after:rite: How do you feel? Mine made me sick for an hour after. There's tea in the dormitory.
lines.after:shape: You fought well. You also hit poor Isa rather hard; I've sent bread.
lines.after:discipline: You looked happy with the new techniques. It suits you. Come and show me the second one later?
lines.after:line: Whoever went with you: I've put tea by their bunks. And yours.
lines.after:project: Twice into the Green and twice back. Sit down; you've gone a colour.

lines.greet: {my_name}. You're a {your_shape}, or you will be. It's in how you stand. Don't look so surprised; reading people is the first thing a field does.
lines.after:hold: Your guard came up late on the left. Twice. You're welcome.
lines.after:rite: Called it. Well. Half called it. The bowl reads things you don't show; that's the point of it.
lines.after:shape: You lead with the same shoulder every time. Fix it before the Examination. Everything in the Green reads shoulders.
lines.after:discipline: You use the first technique too much and the third not at all. The third is the one that wins.
lines.after:line: You held the post from the front. Hold it from the side next time; the wolves come round, not through.
lines.after:project: Projected. Good. Now your weaknesses reach two paces further too. Think about that before the Gate.

lines.greet: {my_name}! {my_city}! Want to spar? Not now, the wards in the quad are thin. Later. Definitely later.
lines.after:hold: I asked Bask if I could take Millstone without the guard. He said no. He said it in a way I've decided means yes.
lines.after:rite: Want to see if our geniuses will fight? Not now. Later. Definitely later.
lines.after:shape: Spar me. Now. Fine, later. But soon. I've been working on a thing.
lines.after:discipline: THREE techniques. I have three techniques. Spar me. Later. Yes.
lines.after:line: Take ME next time. I will not die. I've decided.
lines.after:project: THE FIELD GOES PAST THE SKIN. Did you know? I didn't know. Everything is different now.

lessons.title: Hold
intro: Hold is the first thing and the last thing. Before the stance, before the techniques, before the Pattern: you hold your field in, and you hold your guard up.

A child whose field is waking leaks. Will comes off you like lamplight off a window, and the molted things on the line can smell it from a mile out. That's why the cut-wolf came for you, {name}. Not bad luck. You were shining.
So. First you stop shining. Then Millstone bites, and you hold.

steps.title: Contain
steps.text: Your Will is the blue bar under your health. Stand still, breathe, and draw it back in. [b]Do nothing[/b] until it is full.

steps.title: The guard
steps.text: Millstone will come at you now. When he winds up he glows red and a [b]![/b] rises over him. [b]Hold right click[/b] to take the bite on your guard. Block three bites.

notes.hurt: Bitten. The wards took it. Get the guard up before he lunges, and face him.
notes.parry: A parry: that is the next lesson, and it counts.

steps.title: The parry
steps.text: Holding the guard costs Will. A parry costs nothing and gives Will back: [b]tap right click just as the bite lands[/b]. Millstone reels when you do. Parry three bites.

notes.block: Blocked: you raised it too early. Wait for the lunge, then tap.
notes.hurt: Too late. Watch the glow: tap as it peaks.

steps.title: Hold
steps.text: Now the drill. Millstone will not stop. Take [b]five bites in a row[/b] on your guard or your parry without one getting through. Dodging ([b]Space[/b]) does not break the count.

outro: You'll do this every morning of the term, and on the line you'll do it with your life. Go and eat. Varga will want you rested for the hearth.

lessons.title: Shape
intro: Every Shape has a stance. It is not a pose; it is what your field does when you stop holding it in and let it stand. An Anchor's weighs a tonne. A Cast's goes thin and fast. Yours is yours.
And every Shape has its first technique: the thing your body did on the night the field woke, before anyone taught you anything. Today you do it on purpose, until it is boring.
Then the ladder. Three of your cohort, one after another, inside the wards. Nobody gets hurt in here. Everybody remembers who won.

steps.title: The stance
steps.text: Press [b]F[/b] to take {stance}: {stance_text}. It drains Will while you hold it. Hold it for [b]four seconds[/b] without dropping it.

steps.title: {technique}
steps.text: [b]Q[/b] is {technique}: {technique_text} It costs Will and has a cooldown, so you cannot lean on it. Use it [b]three times[/b] on Millstone.

notes.no-will: Out of Will. Stand still a moment; it refills.

steps.title: The ladder
steps.text: Your cohort, one at a time. Strike ([b]LMB[/b]), guard and parry ([b]RMB[/b]), dodge ([b]Space[/b]), your technique ([b]Q[/b]), your stance ([b]F[/b]), your Pattern ([b]R[/b]) when its Trigger is met, and your genius ([b]G[/b] to change its order). A bout ends when one of you drops; the wards catch whoever it is. Win [b]two bouts[/b].

notes.player-down: Down. The wards took it. Up, and again.

spar.$comment: The ladder: who steps up, in order of temperament (the shy ones first), and how much stronger each rung is.

lines.won: {my_name} is down. The wards catch them.
lines.lost: You are down. The wards catch you; {my_name} offers a hand.

outro: That's a Shape. Not a word on a list: a way of standing, a thing you do, and a cohort that knows it.
Rest. Tomorrow belongs to your city's Discipline.

lessons.title: Discipline
intro: A Shape is what your field is. A Discipline is what your city taught it to do with a weapon, and ours has three things to teach a first-year. Then I will test you myself.

steps.title: Your weapon
steps.text: The weapon you carried from the station was the one to hand. Choose the one you will carry from here: any the {discipline} school teaches.

steps.title: {tech1}
steps.text: [b]1[/b] is {tech1}: {tech1_text} Use it [b]twice[/b] on Millstone.

notes.no-will: Out of Will. A breath; it refills.

steps.title: {tech2}
steps.text: [b]2[/b] is {tech2}: {tech2_text} Use it [b]twice[/b].

notes.no-will: Out of Will. A breath; it refills.

steps.title: {tech3}
steps.text: [b]3[/b] is {tech3}: {tech3_text} Use it [b]twice[/b].

notes.no-will: Out of Will. A breath; it refills.

steps.title: The Instructor's test
steps.text: Now me. Everything you have: strike, guard, dodge, your Shape's technique ([b]Q[/b]), the school's three ([b]1[/b] [b]2[/b] [b]3[/b]), your stance, your Pattern, your genius. The wards are up. Put me down once.

notes.player-down: Down. The wards took it. Up, and again.

lines.won: {my_name} is down, and laughing. The wards catch them.
lines.lost: You are down. {my_name} waits for you to get up.

outro: That is the school's first lesson, and you have it. Carry it well; it carries your city's name.

lessons.title: The line
intro: The line is the one place the Academy cannot ward. So we go out with a rescue team at the post, and with each other.
A party is three. Choose two of your cohort to come. Choose for the fight, or for the company; both are reasons.

steps.title: Your party
steps.text: Choose two of your cohort to come with you.

steps.title: The car
steps.text: The car waits at the Gate.

lines: The car takes you out of Alexandria at lamp hour: three of you, Instructor Varga, and the rescue team riding the tender.
The Green is the line’s gentlest colour. It is still the line. The lamps thin out, and then there are none, and then the car stops at a cutting in the hills.
Varga says: “The post is a mile on. I’ll be there before you. Fell what hunts the cutting, hold the post, and look in on the den if you can. Nobody is a hero tonight.”

steps.title: The cutting
steps.text: Fell [b]two[/b] of what hunts here. Your party fights beside you; [b]Tab[/b] locks on, [b]G[/b] gives your genius its order. Classmates who fall stay down until the post.

steps.title: The post
steps.text: Take the post ([b]E[/b]): whoever is down stands up there, and everyone is whole. Then hold it for [b]forty-five seconds[/b], whatever comes.

notes.ally-down: One of yours is down. The post will stand them up; hold until then.

steps.title: The den
steps.text: The Warden of the Cutting. A second-molt beast, named. Everything you have, and everyone with you.

steps.title: Extraction
steps.text: Back to the line ([b]E[/b] at the way out). The car is waiting, and so is Varga.

lines: The car’s lamps come up the cutting. The rescue team puts away the stretchers they did not need.
On the way back nobody talks much. The Green is behind you, and the window shows your own face in it, and it looks different.
You are down, and the Green does not stop. Then it does: the rescue team’s lamps, and hands under your arms, and the car.
The wards of the Academy close over you like water. You will go out again. Not tonight.

outro: The line took your measure tonight, and you took its. Rest; tomorrow I show you what the field can do past the skin.

lessons.title: Project
intro: Everything you have done so far, you did inside your skin. Hold kept the field in; the stance let it stand; the techniques threw a little of it. Project is the rest.
Take your stance with your Will high and keep it there. When the field has nowhere left to go, it goes out. You will feel it. Then we see what you can reach.

steps.title: Open the field
steps.text: Press [b]F[/b] for your stance and hold it with your Will above sixty. Three seconds, and the field goes past the skin.

notes.no-will: Your Will is too low. Drop the stance, breathe, and take it again.

steps.title: Reach
steps.text: Your techniques reach farther now, and hit harder. Land your Shape's technique ([b]Q[/b]) on Millstone from [b]beyond arm's reach[/b] (more than two and a half metres) three times.

notes.whiff: Still out of reach. A pace closer; the field goes two paces now, not ten.

steps.title: The Field Examination
steps.text: The real one: the Green again, with your field open and a party of three. Varga watches from the post. Choose who comes.

steps.title: The car
steps.text: The car waits at the Gate.

lines: The car again, at lamp hour. Nobody says it is the Examination. Everybody knows.
Varga, at the door of the car: “Field open from the moment your boots touch the cutting. I will be at the post. I will not help.”

steps.title: The cutting
steps.text: Fell [b]two[/b]. Your field is open: your techniques reach past the skin.

steps.title: The post
steps.text: Take the post ([b]E[/b]) and hold it for [b]forty-five seconds[/b]. Varga is watching.

steps.title: The den
steps.text: The Warden. This time it is the Examination.

steps.title: Extraction
steps.text: Back to the line ([b]E[/b] at the way out).

lines: Varga is at the car before you are. She has a slate, and she does not show you what is on it.
“Stage three,” she says, as if remarking on the weather. “Passed.” Behind her the rescue team is already asleep in the tender.
Down. The Green closes over you, and then the rescue team's lamps open it again.
Varga, in the car: “That was the Examination. You will take it again. Everybody who is anybody has.”

outro: Stage three. That is the last thing the Academy teaches your field; the rest it teaches itself, out there.
Tomorrow the Gate: your genius is read, and your cohort says what it saw. Rest.

lines: The dormitory is quiet except for someone in the {your_shape} bunks muttering through a dream.
Your field sits in your chest like a coal banked for the night. The little light that has followed you since the station turns slowly over your pillow, and settles.

next.hold: Tomorrow: the rite in the Hearth Hall.
next.rite: Tomorrow: Lesson 3, Shape, with the Yardmaster. Your genius turns over once in the dark and settles against your foot.
next.shape: Tomorrow: Lesson 4, Discipline. Your city's school takes you.
next.discipline: Tomorrow: the line. The car leaves at lamp hour, and you will not be alone in it.
next.line: Tomorrow: Project. Varga says the field can go past the skin.
next.project: Tomorrow: the Gate. Your genius is read, your cohort speaks, and the line takes you.

rest.too_early: It is too early to sleep. There is work in the yard.
rest.already: You are rested. The day is waiting.

rite.$comment: The rite in the Hearth Hall: the bowl reads your Shape and your genius takes its First Form. The Shape read is the questionnaire's leans (nudged by your spark), plus how you have played the Academy so far (recordLeans: per thing done, toward a Shape), plus the bowl's own noise. A different Shape from the questionnaire's is a surprise; noise is the main knob for how often that happens. The First Form is read from the Seed, the blood and the Shape (data/reading.json, firstFormWeights) plus formNoise.

intro: Everyone else has been through. The bowl is warm. Good.
Your field has been awake a year, {name}, and it has never been asked a question. The bowl asks. Pour yourself into it, all of it, and keep nothing back.
When it has read you, the little light that follows you will go into the fire, and come out as what it truly is.
lines.pour: Hold [b]E[/b] (or the left mouse button) to pour your field into the bowl.
lines.confirm: {shape}. As the questions said. Some of us are what we look like.
lines.surprise: {shape}. Not {was}: {shape}. The questions read what you told them. The bowl reads what you are.
lines.name: It will answer to a name. Give it one.
after: {genius_name}. A {form}. It has chosen you back; it will grow as you do, and it will remember all of it.
Tomorrow you start learning what a {shape} is for.

gate.$comment: The Gate: the genius's Second Form read from how the Academy was played (three candidates, your choice, or settle), the cohort's write-up, Commencement. The write-up is built from the record: each line's test is a key of the record compared to a number.

intro: Here we are. The Gate: the platform the line leaves from, and the last thing the Academy does to you.
Your genius has watched you for a term. Every parry, every order, every time you stood in the yard with the wrong shoulder forward. Now it reads what it saw, and takes a body that fits.
It offers three. Choose, or let it settle on the one that fits best. Either way it is yours; there is no wrong one.
lines.chosen: {genius_name} becomes a {form}. Look at it: that is a term of your life, standing there.
lines.settled: It settles: a {form}. It knew before you did.
lines.writeup_intro: Your cohort has written you up, as every cohort does. They do not know you will read it. Here.
commencement: Commencement. There is no ceremony in it; there is the line, and the car, and the fact that you are on it.
You leave with a Shape, a field at Stage three, a school, a Pattern, a genius with a name, and twelve people who will remember you. That is what the Academy is for.

writeup.text: Quick hands: parries more than they block, and knows it.
Takes a bite on the guard rather than risk the parry. Steady, not showy.
Hard to hit. The yard remembers trying.
Gets hit a lot and does not seem to mind. Either brave or stubborn; the cohort is split.
Took the ladder without a loss, and did not gloat. Mostly.
Lost on the ladder and came back for the next rung. Some of us noticed.
Carried out of the Green once. Went back. That is the whole of it.
Holds a post like it is a doorway with someone behind it.
Talks to everyone. Knows every name in the cohort, and uses them.
Keeps to themself. Those they did speak to speak well of them.
Passed the Field Examination with the field open, first time of asking.

gate.closing: Would found a guild with them. Signed, the Hundred-and-Fourth Cohort.
